prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Warehouse operating boundary: designated receiving interface through release of a completed outbound load from the shipping interface. Pallets remain inside during inspection, identification, buffering, storage, retrieval, and dispatch preparation.
Inbound acceptance requires a valid receipt instruction and a safely handleable pallet. Inbound arrivals must be checked against the scheduled delivery window before door assignment. Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection outcomes before accepted pallets enter storage operations. Pallet Dimension Scanner captures dimensions determining handling/storage eligibility. Inbound Pallet Buffer temporarily holds accepted pallets when storage cannot proceed. Storage locations must support safe handling, efficient retrieval, and required inventory controls.
North Aisle Stacker Crane and South Aisle Stacker Crane perform assigned storage/retrieval in their respective designated aisles. East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor carry pallets along their respective designated transfer routes. Conveyor Line Controller coordinates conveyor movement within its assigned scope. Autonomous Forklift Fleet moves pallets only in approved travel areas under authorized tasking. Yard Gate Controller controls perimeter vehicle access.
Outbound Dispatch Sorter organizes eligible pallets into assigned dispatch sequence. Outbound Checkweigh Scale verifies pallet weight before shipment completion. Shipping Documentation Desk prepares required outbound-load records. Warehouse Operations Supervisor oversees exceptions, operational priorities, and recovery decisions.
Warehouse Management System (alias: Morrowglass) is authoritative for inventory records and warehouse-work release; it maintains each controlled pallet’s authoritative status, location, and handling eligibility. No equipment may begin inventory-moving work without its authorized release. Physical movement and inventory status must be reconciled to keep recorded locations dependable.
Safety Zone Controller enforces movement restrictions in designated protected areas. Fire Alarm Panel provides facility alarm status for operational response. Maintenance Release Terminal records equipment availability for operational planning.
Service objective: accurately process accepted pallets and meet committed dispatch times without bypassing safety or inventory controls. No explicit operating modes specified.

New part:
S028: The Yard Gate Controller records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, and arrival time.
S029: Yard Gate Controller is also known as Velvetrook.
S030: Drivers follow the gate instructions to the designated staging lane while a receiving door is prepared.
S031: The gate process flags unscheduled arrivals for review before they enter the receiving area.
S032: The Inbound Inspection Desk is also known as Cinderbay.
S033: The Inbound Inspection Desk checks delivery paperwork against the expected shipment and confirms the trailer is presented for inspection.
S034: Staff verify trailer identification and inspect accessible seals before unloading is authorized.
S035: Visible damage, mismatched identifiers, or compromised seals are recorded with the affected shipment details.
S036: The Inbound Inspection Desk sends the Trailer Seal Exception Note when a seal discrepancy requires follow-up.
S037: A receiving door is assigned only when the door, staging lane, and unloading crew are available.
S038: Door assignments are coordinated with the current yard position so that trailers do not obstruct active traffic routes.
S039: The Yard Gate Controller directs each cleared trailer from staging to its assigned receiving door.
S040: If a door becomes unavailable, the trailer remains in a safe holding position until a revised assignment is confirmed.
S041: The Warehouse Management System maintains the expected inbound shipment data used during receiving checks.
S042: The Warehouse Management System sends the Dispatch Wave Amendment when outbound planning requires a change.
S043: Receiving staff compare the physical pallet count with the shipment paperwork before unloading is completed.
S044: Pallets with visible damage are kept separate from acceptable stock while the discrepancy is assessed.
S045: The Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection results promptly so warehouse inventory remains aligned with the received goods.
S046: Door occupancy and clearance are monitored throughout unloading to prevent conflicting vehicle movements.
S047: Yard personnel notify receiving staff when a trailer is ready to leave the door and return to the yard route.
S048: Unloading is paused if an unsafe condition, documentation conflict, or equipment issue is discovered.
S049: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor resolves receiving issues that exceed the desk's routine authority.
S050: The receiving process closes after the shipment count, inspection status, and door release are recorded.
S051: Storage allocation begins after the shipment count, inspection status, and door release have been recorded.
S052: The Warehouse Management System evaluates available positions against pallet dimensions, mass, storage compatibility, and expected retrieval demand.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
